cim: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter AI chip export controls
cim_eredeti: Nvidia espionage scandal weakens Huang's lobby against tighter AI chip export controls
szoveg_eredeti:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman US intelligence agencies classify as a suspected Chinese informant. The board has launched an independent investigation. The affair weakens Huang's lobbying efforts against stricter AI chip export controls, with a newly elected Democratic Congress poised to ramp up scrutiny of AI chip smuggling to China and push for tighter restrictions.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang (Huang Le), a former executive at Singaporean data center operator Megaspeed International, in a company-wide memo. This is according to Bloomberg. US intelligence agencies have classified the woman as a suspected informant for a Chinese intelligence service. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly wrote a memo to senior government officials warning about the closeness between Huang and the woman.

As recently as late October, the Nvidia CEO had described the relationship to Bloomberg as "normal." Nvidia's board has now announced an independent investigation led by a committee of independent directors. The Chinese embassy denied the espionage allegations.Ad

Megaspeed operates data centers across Southeast Asia and provides computing capacity to companies including Chinese tech giant Alibaba. US authorities suspect the company serves as a backdoor for transferring export-controlled Nvidia chips to China. A Malaysian sister company reportedly purchased AI hardware containing Nvidia chips worth at least $4.8 billion between June 2024 and February 2026.Ad

The Megaspeed case points to a broader problem. Despite US export bans, billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips are reaching China through smuggling networks in Southeast Asia. Nvidia recently responded with tighter chip tracking. Its "Fleet Intelligence" system logs the location of AI accelerators and is now a requirement for the coveted Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) status in the region, Bloomberg reports. Sharing location data with Nvidia or the US government remains voluntary, though. Nvidia also removed half of its pre-approved Asian buyers from its list earlier this year and capped the resale of computing capacity to Chinese firms at 50 percent.

Washington and Capitol Hill consider these measures insufficient, according to Bloomberg. Nvidia counters that it complies with existing law and that identifying illegal actors is the government's job.Ad

Huang has spent years pushing for Nvidia and other US chipmakers to keep selling AI processors to China. His argument: shutting out the world's second-largest chip market would push China to build an independent and potentially superior AI industry. He made this case directly to the Trump administration and accompanied President Trump on a trip to Beijing in May.

The affair now undermines that lobbying effort. Republican lawmakers had already demanded a briefing with Huang before his admission. After the US midterms, where Democrats won both chambers of Congress, stricter export controls have become more likely. Bloomberg Intelligence notes that the affair weakens Nvidia's bargaining position right as the new Democratic Congress takes over committee chairs in January and plans to scrutinize AI chip exports to China more closely.Ad

Nvidia has a market cap of roughly $4.5 trillion, making it the second most valuable company in the world. Huang built the company without a conventional hierarchy: about 60 people report directly to him, and there is no public succession plan. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon warned that Huang "is Nvidia" and personally pulls most of the strings at the company. Unlike Mark Zuckerberg at Meta, Huang doesn't hold dual-class shares. His stake of just under four percent offers him no protection against removal by the board or shareholders.Ad
